subject: Biology
text: Identify the plant in which emasculation is not required for artificial hybridization. (2026 Board)
explanation: Papaya is dioecious (unisexual flowers on separate male and female plants), so removing anthers (emasculation) before hybridization is unnecessary.
whyWrong: Rice has bisexual flowers and needs emasculation.
Wheat has bisexual flowers and needs emasculation.
Pea is bisexual and strongly self-pollinating, needing emasculation for cross-hybridization.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is not a component of immune system? (2026 Board)
explanation: Red Blood Cells carry oxygen and have no role in immunity; lymphocytes, plasma proteins (complement, antibodies) and bone marrow (a primary lymphoid organ) are all immune components.
whyWrong: Lymphocytes (B and T cells) are central immune cells.
Plasma proteins include complement and antibodies.
Bone marrow is a primary lymphoid organ where lymphocytes are produced.

subject: Biology
text:
Select the option that shows correct statements about the human menstrual cycle:
(i) Corpus luteum secretes progesterone.
(ii) Only FSH attains a peak level in middle of cycle.
(iii) LH surge induces rupture of graafian follicle.
(iv) Luteal phase of menstrual cycle is also called proliferative phase. (2026 Board)
explanation: Corpus luteum secretes progesterone (i, true), and the mid-cycle LH surge causes ovulation by rupturing the Graafian follicle (iii, true). Both FSH and LH peak mid-cycle (ii false); the follicular phase, not luteal phase, is called proliferative phase (iv false).
whyWrong: Both (i) and (iii) are also correct, so this is incomplete.
This omits correct statement (i) and includes false statement (iv).
(iv) is false — luteal phase is secretory, not proliferative.

subject: Biology
text: Select the mismatched pair: (2026 Board)
options: Mega diversity countries in the world – 12
Genetically different strains of rice in India – Less than 1000
Robert May's estimation on global species diversity – 7 million species worldwide
explanation: India alone has more than 50,000 genetically different strains of rice, so 'less than 1000' is incorrect. The other three pairings (12 mega-diverse countries, Robert May's ~7 million estimate, and zoological parks as ex-situ conservation) are all correct facts.
whyWrong: This is a correct, commonly cited figure.
This is a correct estimate cited in NCERT.
Zoological parks are indeed ex-situ conservation.

subject: Biology
text: Pomato was produced by fusing protoplasts of (2026 Board)
explanation: Pomato is a classic somatic hybrid produced by protoplast fusion (somatic hybridization) between tomato and potato cells, bypassing sexual incompatibility.
whyWrong: Pomegranate is not involved in this hybrid.
Pomegranate is not involved in this hybrid.
Pomato involves only two species, not three.

subject: Biology
text: In an ecosystem, different species occupy different levels and vertical distribution of species is found. This is called _________. (2026 Board)
explanation: The vertical distribution of different species at different levels in an ecosystem (e.g., canopy, shrub, herb layers in a forest) is called stratification.
whyWrong: Layering is a plant propagation technique, unrelated to this concept.
Fragmentation refers to habitat loss, not vertical distribution.
Population is a group of one species, not the phenomenon described.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following sacred groves is found in Meghalaya? (2026 Board)
explanation: The sacred groves of Jaintia hills (along with Khasi hills) are found in Meghalaya, traditionally protected by local communities.
whyWrong: Bastar sacred groves are in Chhattisgarh.
Chanda sacred groves are in Maharashtra.
Sarguja sacred groves are in Chhattisgarh/Madhya Pradesh region.

subject: Biology
text: In the following figure, two ways of pairing of two homologous pairs of chromosomes are shown. Which of the following phenomena is expressed? (2026 Board)
explanation: Two different, equally likely orientations of two homologous chromosome pairs at metaphase I illustrate independent assortment, where genes on different chromosome pairs segregate independently.
whyWrong: Linkage refers to genes on the same chromosome staying together, not two different pairing orientations.
Multiple alleles refers to more than two allelic forms of a single gene, unrelated to chromosome orientation.
Incomplete dominance is a phenotypic phenomenon, not a chromosome pairing pattern.

subject: Biology
text:
Match Column-I with Column-II and choose the correct option:
Column-I: a. Biolistic gun  b. Chitinase  c. Ti  d. Ca++
Column-II: i. Bacterial cell  ii. Tumour inducing  iii. Animal cell  iv. Fungal cell  v. Plant cell (2026 Board)
explanation: Biolistic (gene) gun is used to bombard DNA into plant cells (v); chitinase digests fungal cell walls (iv); Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid of Agrobacterium is itself tumour-inducing (ii); Ca++ ions are used to make bacterial cells competent to take up DNA (i).

Incorrect pairing order.
Incorrect pairing order.

subject: Biology
text: The idea of use and disuse of organs for evolution of organism was proposed by (2026 Board)
explanation: Lamarck proposed the theory of inheritance of acquired characters, based on the use and disuse of organs.
whyWrong: Darwin proposed natural selection, not use-and-disuse.
Malthus's population theory influenced Darwin but is unrelated to use-and-disuse.
De Vries proposed mutation theory of evolution.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following statements about plasmids is incorrect? (2026 Board)
options: Plasmids have the ability to replicate within the bacterial cell.
Their replication is controlled by chromosomal DNA.
They are autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA.
They often carry antibiotic resistant genes.
explanation: Plasmids replicate autonomously and independently of the bacterial chromosomal DNA — that is what makes them useful as cloning vectors.
whyWrong: This is a true statement about plasmids.
This is a true, defining statement about plasmids.
Many natural plasmids carry antibiotic-resistance genes.

subject: Biology
text: Which connective tissue connects ovary to pelvic wall and uterus? (2026 Board)
explanation: Ligaments (e.g., the ovarian and broad ligaments) are connective tissue bands that anchor the ovary to the pelvic wall and uterus.
whyWrong: Tendons connect muscle to bone, not organs to each other.
Cartilage is a flexible skeletal tissue, not an anchoring connective band.
Bone is a rigid skeletal tissue, not applicable here.

subject: Biology
text: Microbes commonly used in kitchen are (2026 Board)
explanation: Lactobacillus (LAB) ferments milk into curd, and yeast is used in bread and dough fermentation — both common kitchen microbes.
whyWrong: Penicillium is used for antibiotics, not routine kitchen use.
Microspora and E.coli are not typical kitchen fermentation microbes.
Rhizopus is used industrially (e.g., citric acid), not typically a kitchen microbe like Lactobacillus/yeast pairing.

subject: Biology
text: The features of some structures of the human male reproductive system are given: (i) opens into the Vasa efferentia through rete testis; (ii) carries semen as well as urine; (iii) maintains low temperature for sperm formation; (iv) leads to vas deferens that ascends to the abdomen. Choose the option that correctly matches these features with the structures. (2026 Board)
options: Seminal vesicle, Urethra, Scrotum, Seminiferous tubule
Seminiferous tubule, Vas Deferens, Urethra, Sertoli cells
explanation: Seminiferous tubules drain into vasa efferentia via rete testis (i); urethra carries both semen and urine (ii); scrotum keeps testes at lower temperature for spermatogenesis (iii); epididymis leads into the vas deferens which ascends into the abdomen (iv).
whyWrong: Mismatches several structures with the wrong features.
Mismatches several structures with the wrong features.
Mismatches several structures with the wrong features.

subject: Biology
text: Exploration of molecular, genetic and species level diversity for gaining products of economic importance is called (2026 Board)
explanation: Bio-prospecting is the systematic exploration of biodiversity for commercially valuable genetic and biochemical resources.
whyWrong: Exploitation is a general/vague term, not the specific technical term.
Bio-patenting is legally protecting a discovery, not the exploration process itself.
Bio-piracy is the unauthorized, unethical use of others' biological resources/knowledge, which is different from legitimate bio-prospecting.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is not a component of detritus food chain? (2026 Board)
explanation: Zooplankton feed on phytoplankton in the grazing food chain of aquatic systems; the detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter (detritus) broken down by decomposers like bacteria and fungi.
whyWrong: Dead leaves are detritus, the starting point of this chain.
Bacteria are key decomposers in the detritus food chain.
Fungi are key decomposers in the detritus food chain.

subject: Biology
text: Meselson and Stahl's experiment carried out centrifugation in CsCl2 density gradient to separate: (2026 Board)
explanation: Meselson and Stahl used CsCl density-gradient centrifugation to separate DNA of different densities (normal ¹⁴N-DNA from heavier ¹⁵N-DNA), proving semiconservative replication.
whyWrong: The experiment was not about separating DNA from RNA.
The experiment was not about separating DNA from protein.
The experiment was not about separating RNA from protein.

subject: Biology
text: Which one of the following is not a component required for Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)? (2026 Board)
explanation: PCR requires template DNA, primers, and a thermostable DNA polymerase (Taq polymerase); DNA ligase is used to join DNA fragments in cloning, not in PCR amplification.
whyWrong: Template DNA is essential for PCR.
Primers are essential for PCR.
DNA polymerase is essential for PCR.

subject: Biology
text:
How many of the following features are related to Nirodh, a popular brand of condoms?
(i) Prevention of sexually transmitted infections.
(ii) Phagocytosis of sperms.
(iii) Male contraceptive device.
(iv) Acts as chemical barrier.
(v) Physiological changes in cervical mucus. (2026 Board)
explanation: Condoms like Nirodh are physical barrier devices used by males that prevent both pregnancy and STIs; they do not involve phagocytosis of sperm, chemical action, or cervical mucus changes (those apply to other methods).
whyWrong: Includes false features (ii) and (iv).
Includes false features (ii) and (v).
Both features listed are false for condoms.

subject: Biology
text: A bacterium having radioactive thymidine in its DNA is allowed to multiply in a medium having non-radioactive thymidine for two generations. What percentage of bacteria will have radioactive thymidine in its DNA? (2026 Board)
explanation: DNA replication is semiconservative, so every daughter DNA molecule retains one original (radioactive) strand. After any number of generations, 100% of the DNA molecules will contain some radioactive thymidine, though the proportion of radioactive DNA within each molecule decreases.
whyWrong: This would be true only if replication were conservative, which it is not.
Not the correct percentage under semiconservative replication.
Not the correct percentage under semiconservative replication.

subject: Biology
text: What is the role of histamine released by mast cells? (2026 Board)
explanation: Histamine released from mast cells during an allergic reaction causes symptoms such as vasodilation, itching, and bronchial constriction.
whyWrong: Histamine causes vasodilation, which typically lowers blood pressure locally but this is not its defining allergic role.
Histamine does not stimulate antibody formation; that is a B-cell/plasma-cell function.
Histamine does not directly destroy pathogens.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is used to visualize DNA bands under UV light after gel electrophoresis? (2026 Board)
explanation: Ethidium bromide intercalates into DNA and fluoresces under UV light, allowing visualization of DNA bands after gel electrophoresis.
whyWrong: Acetocarmine is a chromosome stain used in microscopy, not gel electrophoresis.
Safranine is a general biological stain, not used for DNA gel visualization.
Potassium iodide is not a DNA-visualizing dye.

subject: Biology
text: Genetically modified tobacco plants were produced using Agrobacterium vectors. Which property of Agrobacterium helps in carrying nematode-specific genes into the host plant? (2026 Board)
options: Infectious for monocot plant; has Ti plasmid
Infectious for dicot plant; has Ti plasmid
Infectious for plants and animals; has Ti plasmids
Infectious for monocot and dicot plants; has cry gene
explanation: Agrobacterium tumefaciens naturally infects dicot plants (like tobacco) and carries the Ti (tumour-inducing) plasmid used to transfer genes into the plant genome.
whyWrong: Agrobacterium is not typically infectious for monocots.
Agrobacterium does not infect animals.
Agrobacterium's key feature is the Ti plasmid, not the cry gene (which is from Bacillus thuringiensis).

subject: Biology
text: What conclusion can be drawn if the forelimbs of an aquatic animal and a terrestrial animal have similar anatomical structure? (2026 Board)
explanation: Similar underlying anatomical structure despite different functions (homology) indicates the organisms share a common ancestor — the basis of homologous organs as evidence for evolution.
whyWrong: Similar structure does not imply the same habitat.
Different functions despite similar structure is the definition of homology, not shared function.
Analogous organs have similar function but different structure/origin — the opposite of what is described.

subject: Biology
text: In a dihybrid cross, 2400 individuals are produced in F2 generation. Approximately how many will be phenotypically similar to parents? (2026 Board)
explanation: In a dihybrid F2 (9:3:3:1 ratio), the parental phenotypes correspond to the 9/16 and 1/16 classes, totalling 10/16 of the progeny: 10/16 × 2400 = 1500.
whyWrong: Not the correct fraction of the 9:3:3:1 ratio.
This corresponds to only one recombinant class, not parental-type progeny.
This corresponds to only one recombinant class, not parental-type progeny.

subject: Biology
text: What could be the reason of extinction of Abingdon Tortoise from Galapagos Islands? (2026 Board)
explanation: The Abingdon (Pinta Island) tortoise declined largely due to interspecific competition with introduced goats, which out-competed it for food.
whyWrong: The decline was not primarily due to competition within the same species.
Predation was not the primary cause.
Parasitism was not the primary cause.

subject: Biology
text: Interferons are most effective in making non-infected cells resistant against the spread of which of the following diseases? (2026 Board)
explanation: Interferons induce an antiviral state in neighbouring cells and are also used therapeutically to help cells resist tumour progression; they are notably used in cancer/antiviral treatment.
whyWrong: Malaria is caused by a protozoan, not primarily countered by interferons.
Ascariasis is a helminth infection, not primarily countered by interferons.
Pneumonia (bacterial) is not the primary target of interferons.

subject: Biology
text: Which one of the following evidences does not support Darwin's theory of natural selection? (2026 Board)
options: Appearance of new traits by mutations
explanation: Darwin's original theory was based on small, heritable variations and gradual selection; the role of large-effect mutations creating new traits was established later by Hugo de Vries and the Modern Synthesis, not part of Darwin's original evidence.
whyWrong: Branching descent (common ancestry) is part of Darwin's theory.
Small, directional variations are central to Darwin's natural selection.
Survival of the fittest is a core tenet of Darwinism.

subject: Biology
text: Expression of a particular gene helps to identify transformants. What is this gene known as? (2026 Board)
explanation: A selectable marker gene (e.g., antibiotic resistance) allows identification of cells that have taken up the recombinant DNA (transformants).
whyWrong: A plasmid is a vector, not a gene itself.
A structural gene codes for a protein product but is not specifically used to detect transformants.
An intron is a non-coding intervening DNA sequence.

subject: Biology
text: A DNA molecule is 140 base pairs long. It has 20% thymine. How many guanine bases are present in the molecule? (2026 Board)
explanation: 20% T means 20% A (Chargaff's rule), so A+T = 40%, leaving G+C = 60%, i.e., 30% each. Total bases in 140 bp (double-stranded) = 280. Guanine = 30% of 280 = 84.
whyWrong: Incorrect calculation.
Incorrect calculation.
Incorrect calculation.

subject: Biology
text: Select the correct option for the pair of plants pollinated by water. (2026 Board)
explanation: Vallisneria and Hydrilla are true hydrophilous (water-pollinated) plants where pollen is transported by water currents.
whyWrong: Water lily is actually insect-pollinated, not water-pollinated.
Parthenium is wind/insect pollinated.
Water hyacinth and water lily are insect-pollinated despite growing in water.

subject: Biology
text: Match Column I with Column II and select the correct option: a. Primers b. Insertional inactivation c. Bioreactor d. Downstream processing; i. β-galactosidase ii. To separate and purify products iii. Chemically synthesized oligonucleotides iv. Large scale production of specific product of activity of microbes (2026 Board)
explanation: Primers are chemically synthesized oligonucleotides (iii); insertional inactivation is detected via loss of β-galactosidase activity (i); a bioreactor is used for large-scale production of a product from microbial activity (iv); downstream processing separates and purifies the product (ii).
whyWrong: Incorrect pairing.
Incorrect pairing.
Incorrect pairing.

subject: Biology
text: Golden rice is a promising transgenic crop. When released for cultivation, it will help in: (2026 Board)
options: Reduction of Vitamin A deficiency in humans
explanation: Golden rice is genetically engineered to produce beta-carotene (a Vitamin A precursor) in the endosperm, aimed at reducing Vitamin A deficiency.
whyWrong: Golden rice is not a biofuel crop.
Golden rice was not engineered for pest resistance.
Golden rice was not engineered for herbicide tolerance.

subject: Biology
text: Appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of evolution due to: (2026 Board)
explanation: Human use of antibiotics creates a selection pressure that favours resistant bacterial strains, which is a form of artificial (human-driven) selection.
whyWrong: Adaptive radiation is diversification from a common ancestor into varied forms/niches, not this phenomenon.
Divergent evolution refers to related species evolving different traits, not applicable here.
While anthropogenic activity is the source of pressure, the evolutionary mechanism itself is best described as artificial selection.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is not a functional unit of an ecosystem? (2026 Board)
explanation: Stratification is a structural feature (vertical distribution of species), not one of the four basic functional aspects of an ecosystem (productivity, decomposition, energy flow, nutrient cycling).
whyWrong: Energy flow is a key functional aspect.
Decomposition is a key functional aspect.
Productivity is a key functional aspect.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is not a symptom of Ascariasis? (2026 Board)
explanation: Ascariasis (roundworm infection) causes internal symptoms like intestinal blockage, muscular pain, fever and anaemia; skin ulcers are not a typical symptom of this intestinal infection.
whyWrong: This is a known symptom of Ascariasis.
This is a known symptom of Ascariasis.
This is a known symptom of Ascariasis.

subject: Biology
text: Every trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time. What is it called? (2026 Board)
explanation: The mass of living material present at a trophic level at a given time is called the standing crop, usually expressed as biomass.
whyWrong: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass production, not the mass present at a given time.
Not the standard term used.
Ecological efficiency relates to energy transfer ratios between trophic levels.

subject: Biology
text: The smallest part of a DNA molecule that can be changed by point mutation is: (2026 Board)
explanation: A point mutation is a change in a single nucleotide (base) within the DNA sequence, the smallest unit that can be altered.
whyWrong: An oligonucleotide is a short chain of several nucleotides, larger than the smallest unit.
A codon is a triplet of three nucleotides.
A gene is a much larger stretch of DNA.

subject: Biology
text: Some statements regarding drugs and alcohol are given: (i) Adolescents are more vulnerable to peer pressure. (ii) Drug addiction leads to increased tolerance level of receptors in our body. (iii) Alcohol affects the central nervous system. (iv) Excessive use of drugs helps to increase energy. (v) Anabolic steroids decrease aggressiveness. Choose the option with correct statement(s). (2026 Board)
explanation: Adolescents are indeed more vulnerable to peer pressure (i), drug addiction increases receptor tolerance (ii), and alcohol depresses/affects the CNS (iii); excessive drug use does not genuinely increase energy (iv, false), and anabolic steroids increase, not decrease, aggressiveness (v, false).
whyWrong: Includes two false statements.
Omits correct statements (ii) and (iii).
Omits correct statements (i) and (ii).

subject: Biology
text: To separate repetitive DNA from bulk genomic DNA, which of the following methods is used? (2026 Board)
explanation: Repetitive and bulk (satellite vs main-band) DNA form separate peaks/bands of different density in a CsCl density gradient, so density gradient centrifugation is used to separate them.
whyWrong: Elution recovers DNA from a gel, not from bulk genomic DNA.
Southern blotting detects specific DNA sequences by hybridization, not separation by density.
PCR amplifies DNA, it does not separate repetitive DNA.

subject: Biology
text: What could be the reason of extinction of Abingdon Tortoise from Galapagos Islands? (v2) (2026 Board)
explanation: The Abingdon tortoise's decline is attributed to interspecific competition with introduced goats for limited food resources on the island.
whyWrong: Not the primary cause.
Not the primary cause.
Not the primary cause.

subject: Biology
text: A woman having genes for haemophilia on one X chromosome and a gene for colour blindness on another X chromosome marries a normal man. The progeny will show (2026 Board)
options: 50% haemophilic and colour-blind sons, 50% normal sons.
50% haemophilic carrier daughters, 50% colour-blind carrier daughters.
All sons and daughters colour-blind and haemophilic.
explanation: The mother is heterozygous for two different X-linked recessive traits on separate X chromosomes. Since she passes one of her two X chromosomes to each daughter (and the father contributes a normal X), half the daughters become carriers for haemophilia and half become carriers for colour blindness; sons receive her X and the father's Y, so each son gets one of the two X chromosomes (either haemophilic or colour-blind), not both together.
whyWrong: Sons would not be simultaneously haemophilic and colour-blind in this cross as described.
Not all daughters would show both conditions in this way.
Daughters would be carriers, not affected, since the father contributes a normal X.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following is an important parameter for assessing the impact of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth? (2026 Board)
explanation: The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) integrates birth and death rates and reflects how biotic/abiotic factors affect a population's overall growth potential.
whyWrong: Birth rate alone does not capture the combined impact.
Carrying capacity (K) is a resource-based ceiling, not a growth-rate parameter.
Death rate alone does not capture the combined impact.

subject: Biology
text: If a sperm nucleus is injected into an oocyte then all of the following events are bypassed except - (2026 Board)
options: The swimming of sperm to meet the egg in the oviduct.
The sperm's acquisition of motility in the epididymis.
A sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum.
The complex process like cell division and cell differentiation.
explanation: This describes ICSI (intracytoplasmic sperm injection), which bypasses sperm transport, motility, and zona pellucida binding, but normal embryonic cell division and differentiation still must occur after fertilization.
whyWrong: This step is bypassed in ICSI.
This step is bypassed in ICSI.
This step is bypassed in ICSI.

subject: Biology
text: If A = species richness and B = Endemism then biodiversity hotspots have (2026 Board)
options: low degree of A and low degree of B.
low degree of A and high degree of B.
high degree of A and low degree of B.
high degree of A and high degree of B.
explanation: Biodiversity hotspots are defined by both exceptionally high species richness and high levels of endemism (species found nowhere else).
whyWrong: Hotspots require high, not low, values of both.
Hotspots require high species richness too.
Hotspots require high endemism too.

subject: Biology
text: Two plants whose DNA has been sequenced are (2026 Board)
explanation: Rice and Arabidopsis thaliana were among the first plant genomes to be fully sequenced, serving as model plant genome projects.
whyWrong: Wheat's genome sequencing came much later due to its complexity.
Not the pair typically cited as early sequenced plant genomes.
Not the pair typically cited as early sequenced plant genomes.

subject: Biology
text: Antivenom injection is an example of (2026 Board)
explanation: Antivenom contains pre-formed antibodies administered directly to the patient, which is passive immunity created artificially (not by the patient's own immune response).
whyWrong: Natural active immunity arises from actual infection, not injected antibodies.
Artificial active immunity is via vaccination, which triggers the body's own antibody production.
Natural passive immunity is via maternal antibodies (e.g., through placenta/milk).

subject: Biology
text: Pollen grains have a mucilaginous covering on them in most of the water pollinating plants — why is this helpful? (2026 Board)
options: It helps pollen grains to be submerged and transported in water.
It increases pollen grain size for wind dispersal.
explanation: The mucilaginous covering on pollen grains of water-pollinated (hydrophilous) plants helps them stay buoyant/protected and be transported effectively through water to reach the stigma.
whyWrong: Mucilage is unrelated to insect attraction; that is the role of scent/nectar/colour.
Mucilage does not prevent germination.
Mucilage is unrelated to wind dispersal.

subject: Biology
text: Caenorhabditis elegans is a nematode which is (2026 Board)
explanation: Caenorhabditis elegans is a free-living, non-pathogenic nematode widely used as a model organism in genetics and developmental biology (e.g., in the Human Genome Project comparative studies).
whyWrong: C. elegans is not a parasite.
C. elegans is not pathogenic.
C. elegans is free-living, not ecto-parasitic.

subject: Biology
text: Self-incompatibility in some flowering plants is a _____ mechanism that prevents self-fertilization. (2026 Board)
explanation: Self-incompatibility is a physiological (genetically controlled biochemical recognition) mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilizing the same flower/plant.
whyWrong: It is not simply a structural/morphological barrier.
It is not purely a structural/anatomical barrier.
While genetically controlled, the mechanism operates physiologically (pollen-pistil biochemical recognition), the term commonly used in NCERT.

subject: Biology
text: Which of the following traits studied by Mendel in pea plant is a recessive trait? (2026 Board)
explanation: In Mendel's pea crosses, seed colour yellow is dominant over green, making green seed the recessive trait.
whyWrong: Tall stem is dominant over dwarf.
Green pod colour is dominant over yellow pod.
Violet flower colour is dominant over white.

subject: Biology
text: Current percentage of tropical rainforests covering the Earth's land surface is (2026 Board)
explanation: Tropical rainforests, though extremely species-rich, currently cover only about 6% of the Earth's land surface.
whyWrong: Not the correct figure.
Not the correct figure.
Not the correct figure.

subject: Biology
text: All of the following are true with respect to organ transplantation except - (2026 Board)
options: Tissue matching is essential before undertaking any graft.
T-lymphocytes play an important role in graft rejection.
Patient takes immuno-suppressants for first few weeks only after transplantation.
Blood group matching is important before transplantation.
explanation: Transplant recipients generally need to take immunosuppressant drugs long-term (often for life), not just for the first few weeks, to prevent graft rejection.
whyWrong: This is a true, essential step before transplantation.
T-lymphocytes indeed mediate graft rejection.
Blood group matching is indeed essential before transplantation.

subject: Biology
text: Given below are stages of embryo sac formation from megaspore mother cell — the process from megaspore mother cell to functional megaspore, and then to 8-nucleate embryo sac, involves which types of nuclear division? (2026 Board)
options: Meiosis followed by three successive mitotic divisions
Meiosis followed by one mitotic division
explanation: The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to form four megaspores (usually one survives); the functional megaspore then undergoes three successive mitotic (free nuclear) divisions to form the 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac.
whyWrong: Meiosis alone would not produce the 8-nucleate embryo sac.
Mitosis alone cannot reduce chromosome number to form megaspores.
Three mitotic divisions, not one, are needed to reach the 8-nucleate stage.

subject: Biology
text: The recombinant protein obtained from transgenic animals that could be used to treat emphysema is: (2026 Board)
explanation: α-1-antitrypsin produced by transgenic animals is used to treat emphysema, a lung disease.
whyWrong: Humulin (recombinant insulin) is used for diabetes, not emphysema.
α-lactalbumin is a milk protein used in infant nutrition, not emphysema treatment.
Iodothyronine is a thyroid hormone unrelated to emphysema.

subject: Biology
text: The construction of the first recombinant DNA was done by using the native plasmid of: (2026 Board)
explanation: Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer constructed the first recombinant DNA using a native plasmid isolated from Salmonella typhimurium, linked with an antibiotic-resistance plasmid.
whyWrong: B. thuringiensis is used for its toxin gene, not for the first rDNA construction.
Agrobacterium's Ti plasmid is used for plant transformation, not the first rDNA experiment.

subject: Biology
text: Connell's elegant field experiments on the rocky seacoast of Scotland found that larger barnacles Balanus dominated the intertidal area and removed the smaller barnacles Chathamalus. This happened due to: (2026 Board)
explanation: Connell's classic barnacle study demonstrated competitive exclusion — interspecific competition — where Balanus outcompeted Chthamalus for space in the lower intertidal zone.
whyWrong: No parasitic relationship is involved.
No predator-prey relationship is involved.
The species do not benefit each other.

subject: Biology
text: Protein encoded by gene Cry-I Ab controls the infestation of which of the following? (2026 Board)
explanation: The cry1Ab gene's Bt toxin is effective against the corn borer, a lepidopteran pest of maize.
whyWrong: Cotton bollworms are controlled mainly by cry1Ac/cry2Ab genes in Bt cotton.
Bt toxins are not effective against mosquitoes in this context.
Agrobacterium is a bacterium/vector, not a pest.

subject: Biology
text: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on its head are usually observed during which month of pregnancy? (2026 Board)
explanation: By the fifth month of pregnancy, the foetus generally shows the first movements and hair appears on its head.
whyWrong: Too early for these developmental milestones.
These milestones occur earlier, in the fifth month.
Too early for these developmental milestones.

subject: Biology
text: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita are examples of: (2026 Board)
explanation: Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita both develop from the same basic structure (modified stem/axillary bud) despite performing different functions, making them homologous organs — evidence of divergent evolution.
whyWrong: Analogous organs have different origin but similar function, the opposite of this case.
Convergent evolution produces analogous, not homologous, structures.
